About Long Beach

Living in Long Beach

Long Beach is a smaller city on the beach between Gulfport and Pass Christian. In the early 1900s it was known for radish farming; today it is mostly homes, a small-town downtown, and the Long Beach Harbor.

Streets south of the railroad sit close to the water under big live oaks, and neighborhoods north of the tracks run up toward Interstate 10.

Getting around

Roads and commute

US 90 runs along the beach, and Interstate 10 is a few miles north. Gulfport-Biloxi International Airport is a short drive east.

Workers who live in Long Beach spend an average of 23.5 minutes getting to work, one way (Mississippi average: 25.6).

Near the water

Flood zones and insurance costs can change from one street to the next on the Coast. Look up any address on FEMA's flood map, and ask me for help getting insurance quotes before you make an offer.
